cost.q: Does the free web check cost anything?
cost.a: No. A consultation about the result is free as well.

who.q: Can I answer if I am not in IT?
who.a: Yes. All questions are multiple choice and you can choose "I don't know". Detailed questions are optional.

targets.a: AS/400 (IBM i), NEC ACOS and Microsoft Access. Please also ask about Visual Basic systems, low-code products such as WebPerformer, and other office computers and mainframes.

internalOnly.a: A setup used only from the company network is also possible. Where it can be reached from is decided after we hear your company's rules.

itReview.q: Can you explain things for our IT department's review?
itReview.a: Yes. We ask what your review checks (where it can be reached from, sign-in, permissions, records, backups, how it is fixed after the move and so on) and explain along those items. Engineers join when needed.

costTime.q: How much does it cost and how long does it take?
costTime.a: It depends greatly on the number of programs, screens and forms, and on the integrations, so it is settled in the current-system survey (Phase 1). The free web check and the consultation cost nothing.

partial.q: Can we start with some operations or systems only?
partial.a: Yes. We agree on the method and schedule with you in Phase 1 and migrate step by step. You do not have to order the whole project at once.

prepare.q: Is there anything to prepare before the consultation?
prepare.a: You can consult us without it. It helps to have the maintenance and lease contracts, a rough count of programs, screens and forms, and a list of the connected systems and business partners.

vendorSource.q: Our maintenance vendor holds the source code. Can we still consult you?
vendorSource.a: Yes. First, we check with you whether the source code held by your maintenance vendor or supplier can be provided for the survey (contract and cost).

result.q: How can I use the result?
result.a: You see the migration difficulty, the urgency and the priority challenge right away. Use them in your internal discussion. The exact approach, schedule and cost are set in the current-system survey.

ax.a: AI transformation: business transformation that makes use of AI. After the migration, AI agents are added to the new web system to analyze the system and its data, streamline operations and extend features step by step.

webSecurity.q: Is it secure to move a system we used only inside the company to the web?
webSecurity.a: That is a fair concern. A web system also carries a risk: when a weakness (vulnerability) is found in software it uses, that weakness can be exploited until it is fixed. So when we decide how to migrate, we decide with you where the system can be reached from (only on your internal network, or from outside the office as well), how people sign in, and how permissions, records and backups are managed. After the move, we who build it also provide the upkeep to keep fixing weaknesses when they are found; how much you leave to us is discussed with the approach. Note also that once maintenance of the OS or a product ends, weaknesses found in it are no longer fixed, and this applies to your current system too.

data.q: Are the specifications and source code we provide used to train AI?
data.a: No. Specifications, source code and other materials you entrust to us are processed in a secure environment where they are not used as training data.

personalData.q: Can we consult you if the system holds personal data?
personalData.a: Yes. We first ask what kind of data it holds and decide with you how the data is handled.

privacy.a: Only to follow up on your result and to contact you about AX Migration.

noDocs.q: We have no specification documents. Can we still consult you?
noDocs.a: Yes. You can consult us without specifications. We look at the screens, reports and VBA to find out what the tool does.

accde.a: We check the file and tell you what can be done. From an .accde (.mde) file the table data can usually be taken out, but the VBA code and the design of forms and reports cannot. The tool is then rebuilt by checking how its screens behave.

partial.q: Can we move only part of it to the web?
partial.a: Yes. You can move the most used functions first and keep using the rest in your current Access tool.

internalOnly.q: Can we move to the web without making it usable from outside?
internalOnly.a: A setup used only from the company network is also possible. Where it can be reached from is decided after we hear your company's rules.

itReview.q: Can you explain things for our IT department's review?
itReview.a: Yes. We ask what your review checks (where it can be reached from, sign-in, permissions, records, backups, how it is fixed after the move and so on) and explain along those items. Engineers join when needed.

personalData.q: Can we consult you if the tool holds personal data?
personalData.a: Yes. We first ask what kind of data it holds and decide with you how the data is handled. The detailed questions of the free web check also let you choose the kinds of data it holds.

webSecurity.q: Is it secure to move a tool we used only inside the company to the web?
webSecurity.a: That is a fair concern. A web system also carries a risk: when a weakness (vulnerability) is found in software it uses, that weakness can be exploited until it is fixed. So when we decide the approach, we decide with you where the system can be reached from (only on your internal network, or from outside the office as well), how people sign in, and how permissions, records and backups are managed. After the move, we who build it also provide the upkeep to keep fixing weaknesses when they are found; how much you leave to us is discussed with the approach. Note also that versions of Access whose support has ended get no fixes when weaknesses are found.

cost.q: What does the cost depend on?
cost.a: It depends on the number of screens and reports, the amount of VBA, the links to other systems and databases, and the amount and state of the data. We give you an estimate after checking the contents. The free web check and the 30-minute online consultation cost nothing.

period.a: It depends on the size of the tool and the approach. We tell you after checking the contents, together with the approach.

useDuring.q: Can we keep using our current Access tool during the work?
useDuring.a: In most cases you can keep using your current Access until the switch-over day. There may be times, such as when the data is moved, when we ask you to hold off on input. We agree on the schedule with you in advance.

department.q: Can a single department of a large company consult you?
department.a: Yes. We take on a single tool of a single department.

who.q: Can I answer if I am not in IT?
who.a: Yes. All questions are multiple choice and you can choose "I don't know". Detailed questions are optional.

consult.a: It is a free 30-minute online consultation as a rule. Engineers join when needed. You can apply from the result of the free web check, or by phone or email.

calls.title: Import a sales agency's call report
calls.description: Read the agency's call report (CSV or Excel). A row of the same company and agency is updated, otherwise a "Sales agency" row is added (company names match regardless of "Co., Ltd." and full/half width). The file is read on this screen; only the rows are sent.

calls.problems: {count} cells could not be read. Those fields are left empty.
calls.tooMany: Up to {max} rows at a time.

import.title: Import an agency's appointment report
import.description: Read the agency's report (CSV or Excel) and attach each row to a lead by email address (or company name). New hearings are prefilled as "Sales agency". No lead is created.
import.mapping: Columns (choose again when the names differ from the format)
import.needKey: Choose the email or the company column to find the leads.
import.problems: {count} cells could not be read. Those fields are left empty.
import.ambiguous: Rows with several leads of the same company: {count}
import.tooMany: Up to {max} rows at a time.
import.replaced: Rows replaced by a later row for the same lead: {count}
